tile-calculator.name: Tile Calculator
tile-calculator.tagline: Estimate floor tiles, boxes, and cost for any room — with cutting waste included.
tile-calculator.metaTitle: Tile Calculator – Floor Tile & Box Estimator | JaurTools
tile-calculator.metaDescription: Free tile calculator. Enter room size and tile size to estimate tiles needed, boxes to buy and total cost — 100% in your browser.
tile-calculator.keywords: tile calculator, floor tile calculator, how many tiles do I need, tile box calculator, tiles per square meter
tile-calculator.quickAnswer: Divide the floor area by the area of one tile, add your waste percentage for cutting, and round up — that is the number of tiles to buy. Divide by tiles per box for the box count. A 4×5 m room with 60×60 cm tiles needs 62 tiles (16 boxes of 4) at 10% waste.
keyFacts: One 60×60 cm tile covers 0.36 m², so a 20 m² room needs about 56 tiles before waste.
Cutting waste of 5–10% covers edge cuts; diagonal layouts and small rooms need 10–15%.
Tiles are sold by the box, and most shops do not sell single tiles — always round up to whole boxes.
Buy all boxes from the same batch (shade/lot number): dye lots vary visibly between batches.
Measure the room wall to wall; fixed fittings you tile around can be subtracted for large kitchens.
Large-format tiles (60×120 cm and up) need fewer grout lines but are harder to level — budget extra adhesive.
howTo: Enter the room's length and width in meters.
Enter your tile's length and width in centimeters.
Enter how many tiles come in one box (check the packaging).
Set the waste percentage — 10% is a safe default.
Read tiles to buy, boxes to order, and the estimated cost.
For diagonal layouts, raise waste to 15% before reading the box count.
tile-calculator.formula:
Floor area = L × W (m²)
Tile area = (tile L ÷ 100) × (tile W ÷ 100)
Tiles = ceil(floor area ÷ tile area × (1 + waste/100))
Boxes = ceil(tiles ÷ tiles per box)
Cost = tiles × price per tile
tile-calculator.workedExample:
Room 4 m × 5 m, tiles 60 × 60 cm, 4 per box, waste 10%, price 2.5 per tile.
Floor area = 20 m²
Tile area = 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.36 m²
Exact tiles = 20 ÷ 0.36 = 55.56
To buy = ceil(55.56 × 1.10) = ceil(61.11) = 62 tiles
Boxes = ceil(62 ÷ 4) = ceil(15.5) = 16 boxes
Cost = 62 × 2.5 = 155
benefits: Stops mid-project tile shortages that delay tilers and cost extra trips.
Box rounding matches how shops actually sell tiles.
Cost estimate helps you compare tile options before buying.
Handles any tile size, from mosaics to large-format slabs.
limitations: Assumes a rectangular room: L-shaped rooms should be split into rectangles and summed manually.
Does not subtract doors, fixtures, or feature areas — deduct large untiled zones yourself.
Price is a rough estimate: it excludes adhesive, grout, spacers, and labor.
Always confirm the box quantity and shade with the supplier before ordering.
tile-calculator.privacyNote: This tool runs 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.

faqs.q: How much waste should I add?
faqs.a: 5–10% for straight layouts in normal rooms, 10–15% for diagonal patterns, small bathrooms, or rooms with many corners. It is cheaper than a second trip for two missing tiles.

faqs.q: Why round up to whole boxes?
faqs.a: Shops sell sealed boxes, not loose tiles. Rounding 15.5 boxes to 16 guarantees you actually have the tiles — the spare covers future repairs too.

faqs.q: What is a shade or batch number?
faqs.a: Tiles are fired in batches and colors vary slightly between them. Buying one batch (same shade number on the boxes) keeps your floor a uniform color.

faqs.q: Do I measure wall to wall?
faqs.a: Yes. Measure the full wall-to-wall dimensions. For kitchens with large fixed islands, subtract the island's footprint for a tighter estimate.

faqs.q: Does this include grout and adhesive?
faqs.a: No — it estimates tiles only. Adhesive and grout depend on trowel size and joint width; ask your tiler or supplier for those quantities.

faqs.q: Can I use it for wall tiles?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter the wall's length and height as the two dimensions — the math is identical for floors and walls.
